slides.say: A and B represent digits. Which of the following could be the value of A three, times B seven?
We multiply two two-digit numbers with some unknown digits. We do not need to find A and B separately. We'll use the [short pause] product's last digit and its possible size.

[short pause] A three ends in three, and B seven ends in seven. Only those ones digits decide the product's last digit. Three times seven is twenty-one, so the product must end in one. Eight hundred fifty-seven ends in seven, so that choice is out.

Now check the smallest possible product. The numbers are two-digit numbers, so the smallest they can be are thirteen and seventeen. We don't need the exact product: thirteen times seventeen is more than ten times ten, which is a hundred. Ninety-one is smaller than that, so it cannot be the product. This choice is out.

The largest possible numbers are ninety-three and ninety-seven. Their product is smaller than a hundred times a hundred, which is ten thousand. So ten thousand and one is too large. That choice is out.

Only eight hundred fifty-one remains. Let's check it can actually occur. Use twenty-three times thirty-seven. Twenty-three times thirty is six hundred ninety. Twenty-three times seven is a hundred sixty-one. Add them to get eight hundred fifty-one. Choice number two is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
